material_units.source_text: (1) Uncorrelated is not independent: $X$ uniform on $\{-1,0,1\}$ and $Y=X^2$ have $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb E[X^3]-\mathbb E[X]\,\mathbb E[X^2]=0$, yet $Y$ is a function of $X$. (2) Across episodes vs within an episode: in $x_{t+1}=x_t+u_t+w_t$ under a fixed controller, with independently drawn initial states and independent noise sequences, different episodes are independent (independence can fail if the controller is updated from earlier episodes or all episodes share one random parameter), while states within one episode can share past noise and be dependent; this is not automatic, since the fixed controller $u_t=-x_t$ gives $x_{t+1}=w_t$, which are independent for i.i.d. noise. (3) Bounded is not centred: $\varepsilon\sim\mathcal U(0,\sigma)$ satisfies $|\varepsilon|\le\sigma$ almost surely but has mean $\sigma/2$, a bias that no amount of averaging removes.
hypotheses: All probabilistic variables are measurable random elements on the supplied probability measure. Independently drawn complete initial/noise input data means mutual independence across episodes; the controller is fixed deterministic measurable feedback, including predetermined measurable time-dependent feedback.

Uniform noise on the ordinary nondegenerate interval (0,sigma) has sigma>0. Endpoint changes to Icc do not change its continuous uniform law. Its hard bound and mean are distributional statements; every finite sample average has the same expected bias, and iid averages converge almost surely to sigma/2.

Dependence under shared or updated controllers and within an episode is explicitly modal: genuine positive-variance Gaussian countermodels establish that it can occur. The exact reset-controller identity gives independence of positive-time states for iid noise, without requiring independence of the initial state from itself.
